limitations: SPI expresses precipitation relative to the fitted reference-period distribution only. It does not include temperature, evapotranspiration, soil moisture, or crop impacts and is not a measure of agricultural drought damage.

Method: CHIRPS v3 Final monthly window totals; a gamma distribution is fitted per calendar month to the non-zero totals (Thom 1958 approximation of maximum likelihood); zeros are a point mass q = zeros / reference years; the cumulative probability is mapped to a standard normal quantile (McKee et al. 1993; WMO-No. 1090).
SPI depends on the chosen reference period; values are not comparable across different reference periods or precipitation products.
The gamma fit is not goodness-of-fit tested here. Values beyond about +/-2 are driven by the fitted tail and are uncertain, especially with short reference periods.
CHIRPS v3 is a satellite-and-station blended gridded estimate at 0.05 degrees (roughly 5 km), land only. A point value is the value of the containing grid cell, not a gauge measurement.
Published validation covers selected regions. This project has performed no validation of CHIRPS v3 at the requested location.
Station density varies strongly by region and period; sparsely gauged or gap-filled areas are more uncertain (see CHC station-density and fill-map diagnostics).
CHIRPS v3 applies gauge-undercatch correction and is systematically somewhat wetter than CHIRPS v2. Do not mix versions within one baseline or comparison.
Only the Final product is used. Recent months may be unavailable until published.

Anomaly = target window mean temperature minus the mean of the same calendar window over the reference years, in degC (a difference, not a percentage). Window means are day-weighted averages of ERA5-Land monthly means of hourly 2 m temperature.
The reference mean includes any warming trend inside the reference period; the anomaly is relative to the reference-period average, not to a detrended or pre-industrial baseline.
The standardized anomaly divides by the sample standard deviation of the reference window means and is uncertain with about 30 values. The percentile rank is empirical (mid-rank).
Monthly means cannot reveal heat waves, frost, or the timing of extremes, and a temperature anomaly is not a drought indicator by itself; it is context for evaporative demand and crop heat stress.

Anomaly = target window mean volumetric soil water minus the mean of the same calendar window over the reference years, in m3/m3 (a difference, not a percentage). Window means are day-weighted averages of ERA5-Land monthly means.

ERA5-Land is a reanalysis: land-surface model output, not direct observation. Absolute ERA5-Land soil water can be biased in at least some regions, so only the anomaly relative to the reference period is reported, never bare absolute values as truth.
Soil layers: layer 1 covers 0-7 cm, layer 2 covers 7-28 cm, layer 3 covers 28-100 cm. Layer 4 is excluded because its documented depth is contested.
The standardized anomaly divides by the sample standard deviation of the reference window means and is uncertain with about 30 values. The percentile rank is empirical (mid-rank).

Monthly means cannot show the timing of wetting or drying within the window, and a soil water anomaly is not crop-water stress by itself; it is context to be combined with precipitation, evaporative demand, crop stage, and soil properties.
